record.paper_title: On the combinatorics of tableaux -- A notebook of open problems
record.original_question: Consider the treeSYTof (unshifted) standard Young tableaux, with the tree structure generated by containment. For any node with a symmetric shape, there is an automorphism ofSYT(as an unlabeled tree) that transposes all nodes in the subtree rooted at the node and leaves all other nodes fixed. Computation suggests that all automorphisms ofSYTare compositions of these transpose automorphisms (with the identity being the composition of zero transpose automorphisms). Computation further suggests that each node ofSYTis determined up to transpose by the census (cardinalities) of the ranks of the subtree rooted at the node.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let SYT denote the rooted tree whose nodes are all (unshifted) standard Young tableaux of all sizes n ≥ 0, where the unique tableau of shape ∅ is the root, and where the parent of a standard Young tableau T of size n ≥ 1 is the standard Young tableau of size n−1 obtained from T by deleting the cell containing the entry n. Equivalently, the edges of SYT are given by containment of tableaux: T' is a child of T iff T' is obtained from T by adding a new corner cell labeled with the next integer. Regard SYT as an unlabeled rooted tree (i.e. forget the entries of the tableaux and remember only the abstract rooted tree structure).

For any node v of SYT whose shape λ(v) is symmetric (that is, λ(v) equals its conjugate partition λ(v)'), conjugation of partitions induces an involution τ_v of the subtree of SYT rooted at v which swaps each tableau in this subtree with its transpose. Extend τ_v to all of SYT by letting it act as the identity outside the subtree rooted at v. Each such τ_v is an automorphism of SYT as an unlabeled rooted tree; call these the transpose automorphisms.

Let rank_k(v) denote the number of descendants of v at distance exactly k below v in SYT (so the rank census of the subtree rooted at v is the sequence (rank_0(v), rank_1(v), rank_2(v), …)).

Prove or disprove:

(a) Every automorphism of the unlabeled rooted tree SYT is a (possibly empty) composition of transpose automorphisms τ_v.

(b) For any two nodes v, w of SYT, if the rank censuses of the subtrees rooted at v and at w are equal, then v and w are equal up to transposition (i.e., w ∈ {v, τ(v)} for some transpose automorphism, equivalently the shapes of v and w are either equal or conjugate).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a conjecture based on computational evidence in a recent collection of open problems on tableau combinatorics. A web search reveals no published proof or disproof of either part of the conjecture, so the problem appears to remain open.
